flashcard_questions.q: What does it mean to say that business is dynamic?
flashcard_questions.a: It never stands still, because the outside world keeps changing.
Using technology to complete tasks with little human input.
Out of date and no longer wanted because something better has replaced it.

flashcard_questions.q: What is an original business idea?
flashcard_questions.a: An idea that has not been used before to make a product or service.

flashcard_questions.q: What does adapting an existing idea mean?
flashcard_questions.a: Modifying a product so it appeals to different customers or markets.
Sales made through smartphones and tablets.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is adapting an existing idea less risky than launching an original one?
flashcard_questions.a: The product was already successful, so the business knows demand exists.

flashcard_questions.q: Which suitcase did Rob Law create by combining a toy with luggage?
What proportion of UK dog owners treat their pet as part of the family?
What proportion of UK homes subscribed to a streaming platform by 2024?
What proportion of shoppers say they will pay more for greener packaging?
Which product does the lesson give as an example of combining two existing items?
How did McDonald's adapt its menu for customers in France?
flashcard_questions.a: It offers a McBaguette with Dijon mustard.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the risk of relying on new technology?
flashcard_questions.a: If it fails, production halts and sales and reputation suffer.

notes: 15 cards: 6 term→definition (dynamic, automation, obsolete, original idea, adapting ideas, m-commerce), 4 statistics from the lesson (4 in 5 dog owners, 68% streaming, 87% packaging, plus the adapting-risk fact), 4 concept→named example (Art Fry, Trunki, spork, McBaguette), 1 single-fact risk card. Phrased the streaming and packaging cards so they ask for the figure, because the old deck already asked for the category.
